The live background-thread Channel FRAME-SEQUENCE stays the display-gated/deferred leg (zero-retry bar). (desktop-a11y-harness-setup chunk)

- 2026-08-09: When a gate must go live BEFORE the work that makes it green exists, do not choose between a deliberately-red gate and a non-gating warning — pin the known residual as an explicit ledger (an id LIST, never a range expression) and assert it by EXACT-SET equality in both directions. The gate is live and green immediately, and it fails on three conditions: a new item outside the pin, a pinned item that has since been resolved (pin rot — this is what stops the ledger becoming a permanent excuse), and an item that lost its upstream backing. Name the retiring chunk in the pin's doc comment. This is NOT the banned "lower the threshold to pass": the pin records work owed at full precision and shrinks under compulsion, rather than weakening the assertion. (sut-drift-check chunk) **Extended 2026-08-10 (sut-load-envelope): the same shape covers a second, distinct blocker — not "the work does not exist yet" but "the axis is structurally un-derivable from the committed model".** The load envelope bounds sustained RATE x duration, yet `PhaseSpec`/`EmissionSpec` carry no rate or occurrence-count field, so only duration is assertable. Assert the derivable axis, record the other in the artifact as declared-not-derivable with the chunk that will make it derivable named, and pin the exceptions as the same exact-set ledger. One difference matters: these ledger entries carry a REASON string, not just an id, because an exemption is a JUDGMENT rather than a debt — `activity-floor` is exempt because 50 of its 65 minutes are deliberate quiet, and a duration-only bound would have false-flagged the one scenario whose purpose is idleness. A gate that misattributes is worse than a gate that admits its reach: the reason is what lets a later reader tell the two apart. **Extended 2026-08-11 (faithful-emission-dispatcher): the un-derivable axis became derivable, and that is the ledger's exit condition working as designed.** `EmissionSpec` now carries `occurrences`, so a per-phase rate IS computable and the load envelope's rate terms are recorded *derivable but not yet asserted* — the pin did its job by naming the chunk that would dissolve its own justification. Note the two-step: making an axis derivable and re-scoping the gate onto it are SEPARATE pieces of work, because widening a gate's term set moves the exemption ledger for every catalog member at once. Retiring the exemptions and asserting emitting-phase duration is carried as its own chunk; until it lands, the model's per-phase occurrence bound is what keeps an absurd declared rate unexpressible. **Extended 2026-08-13 (dispatcher-determinism-goldens): that chunk landed, and the term it was predicted to assert was WRONG — the ledger emptied by a different bound.** Summed emitting-phase duration leaves `activity-floor` at 900s and `incident-auto-resolution` at 610s, both still over a 600s ceiling, so it retires nothing; summing disjoint bursts separated by quiet is not *sustained*. The gate now asserts the two sustained terms PER EMITTING PHASE (no emitting phase longer than `max_sustained_storm_ms`, none faster than `max_sustained_rate_spans_per_s`) and whole-scenario duration is recorded-not-asserted; under that bound every catalog scenario passes unaided and `[[exempt]]` is `[]`. Two durable lessons for any ledger of this shape: the exit condition must be MEASURED before it is written down (this one named a mechanism that could not deliver its own goal), and when a gate's term set moves, move EVERY consumer of the old basis in the same commit — `check_load_envelope` and `LoadEnvelope::classify` both read whole-scenario duration, and re-scoping only the gate would have let a scenario pass the catalog check while a live run still captioned it environment-suspect. **Extended 2026-08-13 (first-live-green-preflight): third occurrence, and the sharpest — a spec can declare a term `check = "asserted"` (satisfied by construction) for a mechanism that cannot work, and a by-construction term can never catch its own falsity.** `contracts/pulse-run-contract.toml`'s `[incident_formation]` asserted its 45s warm-up "carries the canary service out of Pulse's baseline bootstrap"; the SUT's gate is 3,600s per service, so the mechanism was short by 80× from the day it was written, and the gate that was supposed to guard it passes it unconditionally. The lesson generalizes past ledgers: **when a spec states a term it satisfies ITSELF, the `asserted` check kind buys nothing — measure the mechanism against the SUT's real constant before writing the number, because no gate downstream will.** Corollary on how it was caught: the falsification came from the SUT's own telemetry and source (`cues_emitted: 0` with `services_ready: 0`, then `BOOTSTRAP_WINDOW_SECONDS`), never from Conductor's tests — a green harness proves the harness, and a term about the SUT's behavior is only ever tested by a live leg.

- 2026-08-10: When a gate gains a condition sourced from the PROCESS ENVIRONMENT, read the env at the CALLER and pass the observation in as a typed value — never `std::env::var` inside the gate. Two things break otherwise, and both are silent: every pre-existing test leg starts blocking on the new condition (the var is absent under nextest, so the gate's other arms stop being reachable and their tests pass for the wrong reason), and the only way to test the satisfied branch becomes `unsafe { std::env::set_var }`, which edition 2024 makes unsafe precisely because it races. The fix is to keep the gate a pure function of its inputs: `RunContract::evaluate(&declared) -> RunContractStatus` in `conductor-core` with the env read in `conductor-run`, so tests construct the status directly and both branches stay deterministic with no `unsafe` and no env mutation. Applies to any preflight/readiness condition, not just the run contract. (pulse-run-contract chunk)

- 2026-08-18: When authoring a scenario against a SUT's baseline-relative detector, model the LONG-window aggregation KIND before sizing phases — a windowed PERCENTILE (a t-digest p99 over an N-minute window) ABSORBS a sustained regression that contributes a large share of that window, because the ramp raises its own denominator (measured live: 90s baseline + 90s ramp put ~half the window's samples at the regressed profile, so threshold ≈ long·2.5 ≈ 6000ms while short ≈ 2400ms — zero cues fired), while a slow-half-life EWMA does not (the error-rate spike under the same 90/90 split fired at magnitude ~3.1 with the long EWMA converged near the authored baseline). Detectability under a windowed percentile requires the anomaly SHORT relative to accumulated history; equal halves structurally saturate it, and no threshold multiplier fixes a denominator the anomaly itself feeds. (error-baseline-spike-live-proof chunk) **Extended 2026-08-20 (latency-regression-re-proof): sizing the anomaly is necessary but not sufficient — model the window's ROTATION too, because the detector's sample floor and confidence read a CURRENT-window count that resets on it.** Pulse's long baseline is a t-digest PAIR read as union(current, previous), rotating ~60s on the app's own persist clock: the ≥50-sample floor and `confidence = samples/100` both read `samples_current()`, so a pulse landing just after a rotation cannot clear the floor and one landing just before it loses the window mid-pulse. That rotation PHASE is anchored to the SUT's clock and is not controllable from a scenario, so a single anomaly pulse is a coin flip on it. The fix is structural, not a bigger anomaly: place TWO pulses HALF A CYCLE apart (150s ≡ 30s mod 60), so their phases always differ by half a cycle and at most one can fall in a dead zone. Measured: 31 cues where the prior shape fired zero, with pulse A opening *curious* at magnitude 2.895 while its short window was still baseline-diluted, then `persistence_seconds` resetting 2456 → 68 at the rotation and the next cues going *suggested* at 3.57. Read `persistence_seconds` as the rotation witness — it is a SAMPLE COUNT despite the name, and its reset is the only visible trace of the rotation on a host where the persist-tick line never appears. Keep the anomaly's total under ~1% of the union at the same time: both constraints bind, and satisfying only one still fires nothing.

- 2026-08-18: A field an acceptance grades on must be verified READABLE on the observation surface, not just written by the producer — Pulse's `triage.cue.tick` `cues_suppressed`/`bypass_triggered` counters exist, are written every tick, and read `"<redacted>"` live because the observer's default-deny field allowlist predates them. The five-axis verification chain (existence/direction/representation/provenance/time) gains a RENDERING clause: check the allowlist/redaction layer between producer and observer before grading on any field. **Extended 2026-08-21 (severity-lifecycle live proof): same class, new sites — and the consequence is that the WITNESS MOVES, not that the claim dies.** `triage.incident.auto_resolve.tick` renders ALL THREE of its fields (`resolved_count` / `evaluated_count` / `duration_ms`) as `"<redacted>"`, so the line proves the observer RAN and can never prove it RESOLVED anything — the obvious field to grade was the unusable one. The fix was not a weaker assertion but a DIFFERENT line: `incidents.list_active.request` carries an unredacted `item_count`, whose transition to empty witnesses the same event harder (it dates the resolution). So when the redaction clause bites, sweep the adjacent targets for an unredacted surface carrying the same fact BEFORE downgrading the claim to declare-only — a redacted field is a dead witness, not a dead property.

- 2026-08-19: Pulse keys every buffer table on a content-independent identity tuple — `spans` (trace_id, span_id) · `span_events` (+ event_index) · `log_records` (ts_unix_nano, resource_hash, severity_number) — and a PK collision is a SILENT logged-and-skipped drop, never a wire error. Any emit builder producing N rows per request must vary the key fields per row: seeded per-occurrence ids for spans (the 2026-08-15 canary lesson), and DISTINCT per-record `time_unix_nano` stamps for same-severity log records (a tight build loop can share one nanosecond on Windows; `pii_log_record` now stamps base + index). Verify the landing on Pulse's `duckdb.append` `rows_appended` — it equals the batch size only when no row collided; a shortfall is the collision's only visible trace. (pii-scrub-live-proof chunk)

- 2026-08-20: A magnitude bound alone cannot prove a helper READS a clock — a frozen constant satisfies it forever. When mutation-killing a wall-clock stamp helper (or any read-the-world accessor), assert THREE things and expect none to suffice alone: **magnitude** (a plausible epoch range — both `now_ms`/`now_unix_nanos` end `unwrap_or(0)`, so a mutant returning `0`/`1`/`-1` is indistinguishable from the genuine pre-epoch error path by sign, and only the range separates them); **cross-helper agreement** (mutation replaces ONE helper at a time, so holding a sibling pair to each other in a common unit kills a mutant in EITHER even where its own bound might still be met); and **advance across a REAL pause** (`std::thread::sleep` — never the virtual clock, which the journal basis may not use), the only one of the three that a constant-returning mutant cannot satisfy. Measured: together they killed all six stamp survivors (`lib.rs:517` 3/0, `:631` 3/0); magnitude alone leaves the constant-return mutants alive. Generalizes to any accessor whose value is supposed to come from outside the process. (verifier-self-hardening chunk)

- 2026-08-20: Before writing a killing assertion, ask what the mutant makes DIFFERENT **on the surface you observe** — a mutant survives wherever the harness answers it as agreeably as the correct code. Two measured shapes, both from the read-back seam. (a) **An ECHO stub is blind to a mutation of the value it echoes.** The shared JSON-RPC stub replies with the request `id` it received, so a request-id counter mutated to `-=` (ids `1,0,-1`) or `*=` (ids `1,1,1`) is answered exactly as correctly as `+=` — correlation never breaks and no round-trip assertion can see it. Record the observed SEQUENCE server-side and assert it advances strictly (repeat-free, monotonic); a stale-decoy line emitted before a later response is a useful complement (it kills the pinned-id case by making the skip-loop the carrier) but NOT a replacement — a decreasing counter still pairs correctly. (b) **A one-shot guard needs THREE observations to pin, not two.** Correct code logs once on the first answering call; the `!`-deleted mutant logs on every answering call EXCEPT the first — so at two attempts both produce exactly one line and the assertion cannot discriminate. At three, correct = 1 and mutated = 2, and a single `assert_eq!(count, 1)` kills both that and the emit-nothing mutant. Scope the count by the specific call site's own message text: a helper shared by several call sites (here the read-back key-set witness, called from four) will otherwise let an unrelated site contaminate the tally. **Extended 2026-09-03 (conductor-run survivors): observability is the SECOND question — ask REACHABILITY first, because a site no test can enter produces a green test beside a living mutant, and the plan will not tell you.** Three instances in one chunk, each a remedy named against a site that could not be driven: `execute_scenario`'s interior sits past `probe_egress(DEFAULT_OTLP_ENDPOINT)` and `Dispatcher::connect(…)`, where the endpoint is a fixed `const`, so entering it means binding the SUT's own port — and the plan had named an existing test as the vehicle when that test calls the classifier and the record-builder DIRECTLY and never enters the mutated fn at all (its assertion would have pinned a literal the test itself wrote); `preflight`'s guard needs a connected client from a spawned sidecar binary absent on a hermetic host; and a crate-private fn is unreachable from `tests/*.rs` whatever stubs live there, so an existing integration-tier stub is NOT available to it. So before prescribing a kill, answer three things about the SITE: can a test call it (visibility), can control REACH it (what gates sit above it — a fixed endpoint, a spawned binary, a crate-private constructor), and does the named vehicle actually ENTER the mutated function (read its body, never its name). Where reach costs a host precondition or a production signature change, accepted-deliberate against a cited rule is the honest exit and the score is unaffected — the plan's own escape hatch, not a failure.

- 2026-09-01: **A stub that is faithful in SHAPE can still be unfaithful in FIELD NAMES, and that failure is silent — it degrades to empty rather than erroring, so every stub test stays green while the live path reads nothing.** The shared read-back stub emitted the incident item key as `id`; the live sidecar emits `incident_id`. A reader keyed on `id` extracted an EMPTY active set from a POPULATED live corpus — indistinguishable downstream from a genuinely empty corpus, which is the very false-pass-as-empty class the read-back rules already ban, arriving through the MOCK instead of the data dir. Cost four live legs: three incidents were active 131-142s each while the leg logged `[]`, and the same one-key bug had to be fixed at THREE sites (the library helper, the test's own local copy of it, and the stub itself) because fixing one left the others answering just as agreeably. This EXTENDS the 2026-06-27 stub-fidelity rule (`verification-harness.md`: the stub must emit Pulse's RAW `tools/call` shape, since the rmcp-server stub HID the envelope bug) one level down: envelope fidelity is necessary and not sufficient — the ITEM-level key names are part of the contract too. Two practices follow. Pin the live key in a test that fails if the stub drifts back (`lifecycle_harvest::the_live_item_key_is_incident_id`), and make readers accept BOTH keys the way `conductor-verify::incident_ids` already did — its tolerance is why the shipped extractor never had this bug while new code did. And when a live read returns empty against a corpus you believe is populated, DUMP THE RAW WIRE VALUE before theorising: nothing else separates "the SUT never exposed it" from "our reader extracted nothing", and I spent four legs on the wrong hypothesis for want of one printed line. (p-075-assert-round chunk)

- 2026-09-01: **An assertion that reports only a COUNT names no defect, and a red that names nothing can sit unexplained indefinitely.** The shipped a11y gate asserted `violations.length` toBe(0), so when it went red the failure said `expected 1 to be 0` — the rule, its impact and its 18 nodes were recoverable only by re-running the leg and decoding the driver log, and in the meantime the count was the ONLY thing any artifact recorded about it. Assert on the rendered FINDINGS (id, impact, node count, help text joined into the expected-empty string), so a failure is self-describing. Two sibling traps in the same family, both hit the same session: a failure message that dumps an unbounded subject is equally unusable (an `activeElement` identity helper falling back to `textContent` printed the entire rendered document — bound it to an accessible name, else a short slice for interactive elements, else the tag name); and an assertion can go VACUOUS when the property it reads moves (`isEnabled()` on a control that switched from the native `disabled` attribute to `aria-disabled` passes unconditionally — assert the signal the code actually sets). **Extended 2026-09-04: the same vacuity hits a subject-absent SKIP GUARD, and it fails OPEN.** The a11y suite skips its operator-checklist spec on `$('[role="status"]').isExisting()`, standing in for "a hold is raised" — sound only while the checklist roll-up was the app's only `role="status"`. Adding two a11y-plan-mandated live regions elsewhere satisfied the probe, the skip stopped firing, and the spec then asserted checkboxes it found none of. A guard that probes a TOKEN as a proxy for a STATE breaks when anyone legitimately adds that token — key the guard on the state's own subject (here `[role="alertdialog"]`), and treat a green suite as no evidence that its guards still discriminate. The rule generalises past a11y: whatever a gate observes, its failure must say WHAT it observed.

- 2026-09-02: **A gate whose subject the environment does not supply asserts nothing — give it a seeded subject, keep that subject's CONTENT in a committed file, and pin the file's MEANING with a production-reader round-trip.** Measured on the webview coverage lamps: `/runs/` is gitignored, so on a clean tree the app launches with zero run records, every coverage row reads "Not yet run", and the populated-lamp assertion has no subject at all — while on a dev host it would have passed off ~60 uncommitted local journals, which is the artifact-freshness trap wearing a green hat. Three parts, and the third is the one that is easy to skip. (1) SEED the subject from the harness: `wdio.conf.ts` copies the fixture into a gitignored runs dir and sets `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR` on the driver spawn — repo-relative, because `resolve_under` rejects absolute handles. (2) Keep the fixture's RECORD CONTENT in a COMMITTED file under `crates/`, never inline in the harness config: a journal hand-written into `wdio.conf.ts` is an artifact nobody reviews. (3) PIN its semantics with a Rust test that copies-then-reads it through the PRODUCTION reader (`conductor_core::read_run_journal`, what `run_report` single-sources) and asserts the properties the consuming e2e depends on — here that one P-ID is named by two records whose lamps differ. Without (3) a persist-side change can leave the file parseable but semantically inert, and the e2e stays green over a fixture that stopped testing anything: **a parse failure is loud, a semantic drift is not.** Build the fixture so the assertion can fail — a collision whose two lamps agree would pass under any collision rule and prove none. (live-per-p-id-verdict-lamps chunk, operator directive)

- 2026-09-02: **A test whose subject is AGREEMENT between two surfaces must compare the two subjects to EACH OTHER — comparing each against a hand-written literal is two tests, not a parity test, and its name will claim otherwise.** The shipped `path7_tauri_persists_the_same_blocked_envelope_as_the_cli` never ran the CLI: it drove the Tauri composition into its OWN `TempDir` and asserted `state`/`verdict`/`seed` against literals, with a comment asserting that "cli_smoke proves" the other side. Both tests were green, both were correct about their own surface, and nothing anywhere proved the two agreed — so the capability (v2-25) was measurably unmet behind a green test carrying its name. The shape that actually tests it: drive BOTH surfaces into ONE artifact store (here one `runs.db` under a shared `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR`), read both results back, and assert field equality BETWEEN them, rendering every divergent field in one message rather than failing on the first. Two riders. Make the shared handle LOAD-BEARING — point it at a NON-default location (`shared-runs`, not `runs`), so a handle that were ignored makes the read-back find nothing instead of silently passing on each surface's default. And EXCLUDE the per-run identity/wall-clock fields (`run_id`, `journal_emitted_at`, `read_back_observed_at`, `latency_ms`) explicitly: parity is field equality, never artifact identity, and asserting the whole row would contradict the SLO measurement definition. Generalizes past parity — whenever a test's NAME asserts a relation, check that its BODY observes both relata. (cross-surface-envelope-parity chunk)

- 2026-09-03: **`cargo mutants --output {dir}` writes its tallies to `{dir}/mutants.out/` — the tool always creates its own directory INSIDE `--output`, so a pre-existing output directory is stale by construction and reading the obvious path can hand you a confident, wholly false verdict.** Measured: the repo-root `mutants.out/` left by an earlier run reported `missed.txt` empty and 38 caught — a clean sweep — while the run just completed had 19 missed, its real tallies one level down in `mutants.out/mutants.out/`. Nothing but mtime separated them, and the two readings were caught only because the run's own summary line contradicted the file counts. So: point `--output` at a FRESH per-run directory **under the build dir the repo already ignores (`target/…`)** — a repo-root output dir is NOT gitignored (only `mutants.out/` and `mutants.out.old/` are, by NAME), so a wrap's `git add -A` commits megabytes of tier logs; the same holds for any probe output redirected to a file (`cargo audit > target/audit.txt`). Verify with `git check-ignore -q {path}` rather than assuming, and note that a second run over the same file needs a second fresh dir, since re-using the first is stale by construction. Then read the verdict from the NESTED tallies (`missed.txt` empty + every named survivor in `caught.txt`), never from whatever sits at the path you passed — and never from the exit code, which §4 already pins as uninformative in both directions. Budget from the measured cost, not a guess: 43 mutants over `conductor-tauri` took **4 m 18 s at `--jobs 2`** (a per-mutant rebuild against the Tauri tree), where the plan's ceiling had assumed 90 minutes. (mutation-tier-restored-for-conductor-tauri chunk)

- 2026-09-03: **A mutation survivor classified TIMEOUT is usually a HANG, not an unobserved return — and the fix is in the TEST's await, not in a new assertion.** A mutant that stops a channel/oneshot ever being sent leaves any test awaiting that value blocked forever; the runner reports the whole binary as a timeout, so the assertion that WOULD have failed never gets to report, and a sibling test that already contradicts the mutant is masked with it. Bound every await a decision must arrive on (`tokio::time::timeout`, generous enough not to flake, short enough to fail fast) and the timeout becomes a caught failure naming the undelivered value. Measured on this crate's hold gate: three timeout survivors across two shipped tests went to ZERO with no new test written — one shipped test already asserted the negative case and could not be heard. Read the classes differently: a MISSED survivor means the harness observed the mutant and shrugged (strengthen the assertion — the 2026-08-20 entry above); a TIMEOUT means the harness never got to observe at all (bound the wait). Corollary for the tier's read-out: an accepted-deliberate survivor by construction SURVIVES, so a run carrying one can never have an empty `missed.txt` — gate on `missed.txt` matching exactly the run's accepted set, never on it being empty. (conductor-tauri survivors dispositioned) **Extended 2026-09-05 (audit-corrective): the file you EXCLUDE from bounding, on a judgment about how it terminates, is where the hang lives.** The plan bounded the read-back tests but left `tests/jsonrpc_line_bound.rs` out, reasoning it 'terminates on a decode error'; both `jsonrpc.rs` timeout mutants in fact hang exactly there, because its stub replies only AFTER reading a request line — so `write_message → Ok(())` leaves it silent forever and `!=` → `==` makes the client skip the one reply it would get. Bounding that file's two awaits took timeouts 2 → 0. A termination judgment about a test is a claim about the mutant's behaviour too: bound every await on the seam, and let the tier tell you which one mattered.

- 2026-09-03: **An accepted-deliberate classification covers exactly the code the cited rule's mechanism lives in — it does NOT inherit up to the enclosing function, and a ratified roster can be over-broad.** The `declares` class was ratified at six members against the env-at-the-caller rule; two of them fell to a single ordinary test, because the `std::env::var` read is in `declares` itself while `observe_run_contract` merely calls it — so the enclosing fn's whole-body mutant, and the always-`true` arm, were never the branch that rule forecloses. Killing them needed no `unsafe`, no env write, and no fixture: a contract term naming an env var guaranteed UNSET makes the pure evaluator return a non-empty result where the mutant's `Default` returns an empty one. Two consequences. When classifying, name the exact mutants the mechanism reaches and re-read the fn body to confirm it is the mechanism's home; and when a later chunk touches an accepted class, re-run it rather than carrying the count forward — a roster is a ledger of owed work, so it should shrink under compulsion, and only a re-run can shrink it. Record the roster as the enumerated SET, never as a count, so a stale number cannot outlive the membership. (conductor-run composition-root survivors dispositioned)

- 2026-09-03: **A host-path negative test must WORD-ANCHOR its drive-letter token — `\b[A-Za-z]:[\\/]`, never the bare `[A-Za-z]:[\\/]` — because a `scheme://` URL satisfies the unanchored form.** The `p:/` inside `http://127.0.0.1:4317` matches it, so a test asserting that its subject leaks no host path FAILS on that subject's own correct output. Verified over seven cases: the anchored form rejects a loopback endpoint and a bare URL while still catching a backslash path, a forward-slash path, a JSON-escaped `C:\\Users\\…`, and the extended-length `\\?\D:\` form. The sibling host-path anchors (`%APPDATA%`, `/Users/`, `/home/`, `.cargo`, `.rustup`) need no anchoring — only the drive-letter one collides with a URL scheme, which is why a hygiene assertion that passes on every other token can still be wrong on this one. (live-pulse-preconditions-probed chunk, operator review)

- 2026-09-05: **A per-unit survivor list produced by a `--shard` run belongs to the SHARD, not to the unit — so an audit's "this file's survivors" section is a floor, and re-running the file whole can surface survivors the audit never named.** Measured on `conductor-core/src/obs.rs`: the boundary-#4 audit ran `--shard 1/4` and reported 126 mutants for that file; the file-scoped re-run generated **203** and exposed 7 survivors absent from the audit's list entirely (`install_panic_hook`, `ObsWriterGuard::flush`, `unix_millis` ×2, three `JsonVisitor::record_*` arms). Nothing was wrong with either run — sharding partitions the mutant population, and a shard's tally is complete only for the mutants it drew. Two consequences. Read a sharded audit's per-unit list as **consulted-but-partial**, never as the unit's survivor set, and say which basis a disposition rests on; and when a chunk targets one file's survivors, re-generate that file's mutants whole before claiming its set is closed — the acceptance here held (none of the 7 sat in the targeted function), but only the whole-file run could show that. Owner for the 7: the next audit boundary's full-crate tier. (audit-corrective)

- 2026-09-06: **A typed parse does NOT prove key presence — serde reads an ABSENT `Option` field as `None`, with no `#[serde(default)]` needed.** Measured on serde 1.0.229 against a faithful `RunRecord` mirror (plain derive, no field attributes) with four controls: all 11 keys -> `Ok`; the 5 `Option` keys ABSENT -> **`Ok`** with those fields `None`; the required key `seed` absent -> `Err(missing field seed)`; an extra unknown key -> `Ok`. So a round-trip or `from_str` assertion settles SHAPE and the closed enum sets, never that a nullable key is PRESENT — a conformance check that means presence needs its own `serde_json::Value` key-set assertion beside the typed parse. The corollary is the negative arm: an arm that removes a REQUIRED key is caught upstream by the typed parse and therefore never exercises the presence check at all, so the arm that proves it must remove an **`Option`** key. (The fourth control is also why `deny_unknown_fields` is a deliberate choice rather than a default: unknown keys pass, which is what keeps a documented extension point open.) Caught at a P5 review after the plan had asserted the opposite as load-bearing across three acceptance criteria.

- 2026-09-06: **When you fix a defect in one reader of a shared artifact, enumerate every OTHER reader of that artifact before calling it closed — the same wrong assumption usually lives in siblings nobody looked at.** The run journal carries two record shapes; `conductor_core::read_run_journal` parsed every line as the envelope and failed outright on a run that graded checks (`conductor report <id>` -> exit 1, `missing field seed`). Fixing it was not the end: the harness `status` verb in BOTH shells carried the identical single-shape assumption (`tail -n 1` / `Select-Object -Last 1`), silently reporting a `CheckRecord`'s fields as the envelope at exit 0 (`seed: null`, `slo_tier: null`) — three readers, one class, and the second and third were found by RUNNING the harness rather than by review. Two practices follow: when an artifact gains a second record shape, grep for every consumer of that artifact (not only the ones the chunk names) and check each against the new shape; and prefer a shared discrimination rule the readers call over per-reader parsing, so the next reader inherits the fix instead of repeating the bug.

- 2026-09-06: **A cargo test binary's CWD is its OWN PACKAGE ROOT, so a CWD-relative path constant cannot resolve from an integration test — and the failure looks like a missing file, not a wiring bug.** `CapabilityManifest::default_path()` returns `PathBuf::from("contracts/pulse-capabilities.toml")` and its own doc says the `conductor-cli` / Tauri edge resolves it under the current dir "never this module"; a `crates/conductor-report/tests/*.rs` binary runs with CWD `crates/conductor-report/`, where no `contracts/` exists. Resolve committed repo-root artifacts from `Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../<path>")` — the idiom already shipped at three `conductor-core` sites (`capability_manifest.rs` · `coverage.rs` · `drift.rs`). The trap bites EVERY file-reading arm of such a test, not just the one you noticed: a gate reading both a manifest and a committed artifact needs the fix twice, and fixing one leaves the other failing for a reason unrelated to what the gate asserts. (coverage-completeness-gate chunk; the manifest arm was caught at an operator P5 review after the artifact arm had already been written up.)

- 2026-09-06: **A test that byte-compares a COMMITTED generated artifact against its production renderer needs a line-ending pin, or it is host-dependent by construction.** `CoverageMatrix::render()` is `writeln!`-built (LF) and `write()` stores it verbatim, so the equality holds only where checkout preserves LF — and this repo had NO `.gitattributes` while `core.autocrlf=true` and both CI jobs run `windows-latest` **[corrected 2026-09-07 (a11y-ci-gate): THREE jobs now — `rust` and `frontend` on `windows-latest`, plus `a11y` on an explicit label; every one is still a Windows runner, so the LF argument below is unaffected]** **[corrected 2026-09-17 (`a11y-routine-arm-terminal-on-the-measured-configuration`): that explicit label is now `windows-2022`, moved from `windows-2025` onto the configuration the arm is measured green on (run 35208593666). The LF argument is still unaffected — all three jobs remain Windows-hosted — which is why this is a label correction and not a change to the entry's claim]**. Pin the artifact (`<path> text eol=lf`) rather than normalising endings inside the comparison: normalising is weaker, because it hides a real ending regression the gate should catch. Verify the pin is in force with `git check-attr text eol -- <path>` (expect `text: set` / `eol: lf`) — the file merely existing proves nothing. **Extended 2026-09-13 (`audit-debt-retired-before-epoch-1-closes`): the CONTROL in that check has changed, because there is no unpinned sibling left.** `.gitattributes` now opens with a repo-wide `* text=auto eol=lf`, so an arbitrary tracked file reads `text: auto` / `eol: lf` rather than `unspecified`, and the discriminator is `text: set` (an explicit rule) vs `text: auto` (the wildcard) — both resolving `eol: lf`. The explicit `coverage-matrix.md` rule is kept for exactly this reason: it survives any later narrowing of the wildcard, so the gate's guarantee does not silently become a side effect of a repo-wide default. Measured basis for the wildcard: `core.autocrlf=true` in the SYSTEM gitconfig, `git ls-files --eol` 3031 `i/lf` · 13 `i/none` · 4 `i/-text` with no `i/crlf` and no `i/mixed` (nothing renormalizes), and the `LF will be replaced by CRLF` warning going from every touched file to 0. Corroborating signal that the risk is live, not theoretical: `git diff` prints `LF will be replaced by CRLF` for every tracked text file the pin does not govern. (coverage-completeness-gate chunk, operator P5 review.)

- 2026-09-07: **A nextest filter expression that matches NOTHING reads as success at a glance — `0 tests run: 0 passed, N skipped` with no failures listed.** Measured: `-E 'test(delegated_timing)'` selected zero tests (the binary is `delegated_timing_harvest`, and `test(...)` matches the TEST name, not the binary), so the harvest suite would have been recorded green while it had not executed; the correct selector is `binary(delegated_timing_harvest)`. The exit code does discriminate here (nextest returns 4 = NO_TESTS_RUN, not 0), which makes this the one filter-miss shape a bare `$?` catches — but only if the exit is read from the BARE command, and the printed summary is what names the cause. So after any filtered run, assert the test COUNT is non-zero and matches what the filter should have selected, never just the absence of FAIL lines. **[RECURRED 2026-09-07, same day, `2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed` — this entry existed and did not prevent it.** A plan Test Command was authored as `cargo nextest run -p conductor-run journal_conformance`; a BARE positional argument to `nextest run` is a name FILTER, not a target selector, so it selected nothing — `exit 4`, `0 tests run: 0 passed, 195 skipped`. The target form is `--test journal_conformance`, which `ci.yml` itself already used. Two things generalize. The recurrence was in a PLAN, authored at a phase where no gate re-runs commands, so the entry's "after any filtered run, assert the count" advice had no reader at the moment the mistake was made — a learning that fires only at execution cannot protect an authoring step. And the two failure shapes now differ: `-E 'test(...)'` mis-selects, while a bare positional is silently interpreted as a filter at all. Remedy is a CHECK, not more advice: the plan-authoring gate should reject a `nextest run` line whose selector is a bare positional, since the target form is always available and unambiguous.]** Same family as the mutation-tier rule above (`Found 0 mutants` exits 0 with only a WARN): a selector that selects nothing is the quiet failure mode of every test-selection tool. (halo-hue-budget-re-driven chunk)

- 2026-09-08: **A probe that samples ONE of several candidate artifacts must bound its selection by FRESHNESS and scan every match — a `-First 1` pick reads whichever the filesystem hands back, which is usually a prior run's residue.** Measured twice on the WebView2 session probe. (a) msedgedriver creates TWO `scoped_dir` siblings per session (same pid, different random suffix) and only ONE holds the profile, so a single-pick probe has a coin-flip chance of reading the empty one. (b) Fifteen `scoped_dir` directories from earlier runs sat in `%TEMP%`, several carrying `EBWebView`, so the pick was residue before it was ever this run's. The probe consequently reported `EBWebView=False` on a session that had just returned HTTP 200 — an insensitive check, green-or-red regardless of truth, and the kind that reads as a real finding. The fix is two-part and both halves are needed: stamp a `$since` before the subject starts and filter on creation time, and scan ALL matches reporting any-hit plus a count, never the first. Generalises past this tool: whenever a probe's target is created by a process you do not control, assume it makes more than one and that older ones survive.

- 2026-09-09: **An ESTABLISHED command is not a GREEN command — baseline a gate against the exact targets it will run on before listing it as a gate.** The novelty test that decides whether a gate gets a baseline keys on the command's program + subcommand, which is precisely what a long-established command passes; so the question it answers ("has this command been used here?") is not the question that matters ("has it been green on THESE targets?"). Measured: a per-crate runner-portability gate was listed unbaselined because the command was established project-wide, and it went red at implement on a defect that predated the chunk — that crate's integration suite had only ever run under the process-per-test runner, and the sole prior mentions of the shared-process form were its `--doc` arm, which executed zero doctests and so never touched the crate's integration tests at all **[corrected 2026-09-10: the zero-doctest figure is the 2026-06-19 record, not current state — measured 3 doctests in that crate at HEAD, all green, and it is the only workspace crate carrying any; the half the argument rests on is unaffected, since the `--doc` arm still never touches the crate's integration tests]**. A gate whose subject set has never been exercised is unknown, not green. Second occurrence of the unsatisfiable-gate family in three chunks (the prior one shipped a gate that could never pass), so treat "I have not run this exact command on this exact target set" as a blocking authoring condition.

- 2026-09-09: **A criterion asserting an artifact is UNCHANGED needs a signature over its normalized form — component counts and container-wide flag counts cannot discriminate.** Measured: an acceptance claimed a CI job was byte-unchanged while the only probe backing it read that job's step count plus a workflow-wide flag count, both of which hold unchanged under edits that move the job's content; an md5 over the job's key-sorted normalized serialization made the criterion provable, and it mattered the same session — an edit anchor matched twice and would have landed inside that very job had a uniqueness guard not caught it. Generalize past the artifact: when a criterion names a property, its probe must be able to FAIL on that property's negation, not merely coexist with it; a probe that cannot fail is not evidence however green it reads. **Extended 2026-09-12 (ledger-gate-id-space-generalised): the sharpest case is a test that was already GREEN before the change, because its own fixtures instantiate the very shape the change retires — it then passes after any repair, correct or not, and its green is evidence about nothing.** The ledger gate's discrimination arm asserted id extraction over fixtures carrying the retired version prefix while the filter under repair keyed on that same prefix; it passed at HEAD and would have passed identically had the repair been wrong. The discriminating move costs one round-trip and belongs in the chunk, not in the reader's trust: once the fix is green, RESTORE THE OLD IMPLEMENTATION, run that arm alone, and read what it says — a failure naming both the observed and the expected set is what converts "the arm passes" into "the arm discriminates" — then restore and re-run the headline gate to prove no residue. The tell that an arm needs this is exactly that its fixtures are shaped by the behaviour being retired. Distinct from the RED-baseline rule (`verification-harness.md`, 2026-09-12), which validates a gate whose baseline already fails: this one is for an arm green on BOTH sides of the change, where no baseline can discriminate and only the inverse control can.

- 2026-09-10: **`cargo test -p <crate>` runs its targets in SEQUENCE and aborts at the first failing one, so a red invocation tells you nothing about the targets behind the failure — and a claim about what a red was masking is a claim about the BASELINE's target set.** Measured: the red per-crate gate ran the lib target green, aborted at the failing integration binary, and never reached the crate's doctest target; the green run afterwards listed four targets where the red had listed two. The masked set was ONE target, not the two the arithmetic suggests — the other extra target was created by the same chunk and could never have been masked, so the subtraction green-minus-red overcounts by exactly the targets the chunk itself added. Two consequences. A per-crate green is evidence about every target only once it is green; until then the targets after the failure are UNMEASURED, not passing (the sibling of the established-is-not-green rule above — same gate, one layer down). And when reporting what a red concealed, enumerate the targets that existed at the baseline rather than differencing the two runs' target lists.

- 2026-09-16: **A fixture that exists to prove a SWEEP FORM sits inside that sweep's own subject, so its explanatory prose must DESCRIBE the guarded token, never spell it.** The wrapped-gloss control for the scenario-audit gate carries a retired gloss split across two comment lines, and its arm asserts BOTH that the comment-marker-stripped join DETECTS it and that a plain single-line search MISSES it — the second half being what proves the strip-and-join is load-bearing rather than decorative. The header written to explain that trick spelled the gloss on one line, which made the second half false; three gate entries went red on a fixture that was correct in the only way anyone had thought to check, and the failure named the fixture rather than the code. `.claude/docs/session-learnings.md` (the host leaf entry of 2026-09-11 as extended 2026-09-12, the drive-letter-anchor entry) **[corrected 2026-10-07: this cited `.claude/rules/host-win32.md`; that leaf was retired at setup's host re-seed and the entry moved whole to Tier 3]** already states this shape for a hygiene gate's own command text, and it did not transfer because the domain looked unrelated. The facet that is new: **when a fixture's assertion includes an ABSENCE, the fixture's own commentary is a place that absence can be violated.** Write such a fixture's payload and its header as one act, then re-read the header as the sweep would — and prefer a control whose two halves are asserted together, so a header that breaks one of them cannot pass by satisfying the other.

- 2026-09-23: **A capture test that prints under `cargo test -q … -- --nocapture` must buffer its output and write it ONCE** — libtest's `-q` progress marks (an `i` for each ignored test in the same binary) land on the same stdout the test prints to, so an unbuffered first line arrives prefixed with the mark and can split a line a downstream grammar parses; collect into a buffer and flush it from a drop guard, leading with a newline.

- 2026-09-23: **Before a plan names a test fixture framework for a crate's tests, confirm that crate declares it** — `rstest` is a per-crate dev-dependency here (present in `conductor-core` / `-emit` / `-timeline` / `-verify`, absent from `conductor-run`), so prescribing `#[case]` rows for a crate without it silently requires a `Cargo.toml` edit and a `Cargo.lock` line, which contradicts a plan that also states "no manifest change" and gates `Cargo.lock` byte-identity. Where the crate lacks it, plain `#[test]` functions (or one table-driven test) are the in-scope form; add the dependency only as a planned touchpoint with its lock gate adjusted.

- 2026-10-01: **A grep for a span NAME over a Conductor self-obs journal also matches every CHILD line, because children carry `"parent":"<that span>"`** — key a span-start read on `span == <name>` AND `span_event == "new"`, never on the quoted name alone.

- 2026-10-04: **To split an oversized `tests/*.rs` target whose root holds private or byte-pinned items, move the families into CHILD modules under `tests/<name>/` (each `use crate::*;`), never sibling modules or new targets** — a child sees the root's private items, so nothing gains `pub`, the pinned bytes never move and the target keeps its name for every by-file citation; a child module's `include_str!` resolves from its own file, and the root sees a child only through `pub(crate)`.

- 2026-10-08: **`cargo nextest run --profile ci` is fail-fast in this repo, so a RED run under it cancels at the first failure and prints a partial summary (`N/M tests run`), leaving the rest unrun — a failing-first measurement, or a plan step that predicts a red run's summary line or rests on "no other test is red", runs it with `--no-fail-fast`, or predicts only the failing test names.**

- 2026-10-12: **`tokio::signal::ctrl_c()` installs its OS handler on its first POLL, not on the call** — a test that spawns the listener and then raises SIGINT must `yield_now().await` once between them, or the signal meets the default disposition and kills the test process.

Path-scoped rules for the agent-driven verification harness — the `scripts/agent-run.*` driver, the CLI release-gate path, and the MCP read-back / preflight layer.

**Authoritative sources (bound):** `.andromeda/test-plan.md` §3 (Test Harness Contract) + `.andromeda/obs-plan.md` §3 (log format / service identity). The harness consumes the obs JSON log format; keep both sides in sync.

**Critical adaptation — Conductor has NO daemon and NO inbound listener.** `boot` is a precondition probe followed by a preflight gate (not a daemon start) — the probe leads and short-circuits on an unmet subject, skipping the preflight rather than paying it — `status` reads disk artifacts (no HTTP/IPC endpoint), there is NO PID file, and there is no long-running heartbeat. Do not reintroduce daemon/PID/endpoint machinery.

- **`boot`** — precondition probe, THEN the MCP preflight readiness gate. The leading arm is `conductor preconditions`: `:4317` reachability (connect-and-drop, client only), `andromeda-pulse-mcp` resolvable on the inherited `PATH` (a directory walk, never a spawn), and the three `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_*` handles read for an affirmative declaration. **That last subject is SATISFIABLE** — each handle is graded by the KIND of value it carries (`conductor_core::handle_declared`): the PATH-valued `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` by presence-after-trim, the two flags by an affirmative `"true"`/`"1"` through the value-only `flag_declared`. - **Verdict/error wall:** verification outcomes are typed VALUES (`Verdict`/`ReportState` as `Ok`); `Result::Err` is harness-faults only. Malformed child/transport input (`tonic::Status`, MCP errors) becomes a typed `Blocked`/`Fail`, never a panic.

- **Preflight integrity:** never silently downgrade a preflight that RUNS — `agent-run boot` skips the preflight entirely when its leading `conductor preconditions` arm reports an unmet subject (a non-mutating probe, non-zero exit, every subject named). That skip is CONDITIONAL and not a downgrade: each handle is graded by the KIND of value it carries — the PATH-valued `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` by presence, the two flags by an affirmative `"true"`/`"1"` (the deterministic posture; under a real-model scenario's posture — `conductor preconditions --for` — the L4 flag must instead be ABSENT or falsy) — so `handles-declared` is satisfiable and `boot` reaches the gate (measured 2026-09-04: probe exit 0, then `ReadyState` with `ready:true` in both shells). `conductor preflight --json` remains a valid direct entry point. For an invoked gate — each of the gate's FIVE named preconditions (protocol≠`2024-11-05` / missing tool / no incident opened after the canary storm / app-sidecar workspace-key agreement / unmet run-contract terms) surfaces the distinct `Blocked` state with its own host-path-free string, never the generic corpus-empty one. Which run-contract terms bind is selected by the run's L4 posture, and a scenario declaring a posture other than its gate's is `Blocked` at scenario level — never a sixth precondition. A contract term whose truth lives on the SUT's side is recorded `declared-not-observable` and never blocks — blocking on it would claim a measurement Conductor cannot make.
- **Supply chain:** keep `Cargo.lock` committed + un-drifted; never `cargo build --release` or merge without `cargo-audit` (+ `cargo-deny`) green; hold toolchain ≥1.94.1.

- **Subprocess hardening:** spawn `andromeda-pulse-mcp` as a fixed hard-coded program NAME resolved through the inherited `PATH` (never operator-chosen) — the same const also has a NON-SPAWNING sibling resolution (`sidecar_resolves_on_path`, a directory walk returning a boolean-grade fact, never the resolved path); pass `ANDROMEDA_PULSE_DATA_DIR` only via `.env(...)` after rejecting injection metacharacters — never into argv/shell.

- **Artifact hygiene:** never leak absolute host paths or internal struct names into logs / run-report / `runs.db` / committed `evidence/` — sanitize at the `anyhow` edge + the tracing-subscriber field-allowlist.

- **Self-obs never exports OTLP:** the only OTLP is the PRODUCT fault stream to Pulse `:4317`; self-observation is `tracing` JSON to stderr/file (no OTel SDK), every line carrying `run_id`; zero unlogged panics (`std::panic::set_hook`).
- **Wall-clock from `std::time`:** journal/report stamps use `std::time::SystemTime`/`Instant`, never tokio's virtual clock (scheduling-only) — journal-relative SLO math depends on it.

- **Status is never color-alone:** pair every Verdict/ReportState with its ASCII prefix `[PASS]`/`[FAIL]`/`[HOLD]`/`[MANUAL]`/`[RESIDUAL]`/`[BLOCKED]` (cli); color encodes run state, never decoration.

- **Determinism is the bar:** same scenario+seed ⇒ same stream shape (span identity alone is salted per execution on the production path; the unsalted dispatcher tier stays seed-pure); loopback gRPC/MCP stubs only in tests (`start_paused` for scheduling); zero-flakiness — no nextest retries.

Conductor is a modular monolith realized as a crate-per-seam Cargo workspace: the `Cargo.toml` dependency edges *are* the architecture, and a forbidden cross-seam dependency simply will not compile. All engine logic lives in runtime-agnostic library crates that the headless `agent-run` path (the release gate) drives through `conductor-cli` — headless-drivable core, thin shell.

Determinism is enforced in the runtime flavor: the timeline runs on a `current_thread` tokio runtime so the same scenario+seed always yields the same emission-stream shape. Verification outcomes are typed VALUES (`Verdict`/`ReportState`); `Result::Err` is reserved for Conductor's own harness faults, so the report classifies a model-backed SUT by matching types, not catching exceptions. Every SLO is measured journal-relative (`read_back_observed_at − journal_emitted_at`) against the on-disk JSONL journal — the agent-parseable ground truth.
